KS3 · Year 7 · Unit 2

Becoming a Digital Citizen

Textbook Reader (Pilot)

How to use this reader: Use the Tools panel to change font, text size, and theme. Turn on Paged reading if you prefer one section at a time.

What Is Digital Citizenship?

A digital citizen is someone who uses the internet and digital tools in a safe, respectful, and responsible way. Your choices online affect you and the people around you, even when you are not face-to-face.

Key idea

Your online world is part of your real world. The same values apply: kindness, honesty, and good judgement.

Your Digital Footprint

Your digital footprint is the trail you leave behind online. Some parts are obvious (posts, comments, likes). Other parts are hidden (location data, device information, browsing data).

  • Active footprint: things you choose to share, like posting a photo.
  • Passive footprint: things collected about you, like app trackers.

Public vs Private Information

Some information is safe to share publicly. Other information should be kept private or shared only with trusted adults.

  • Public: hobbies, favourite books, general interests.
  • Private: full name, address, school timetable, passwords, phone number.
  • Personal: anything that can identify you, including photos that show your uniform.

Privacy and Settings

Privacy settings help, but they are not perfect. Always think: Would I be happy if a stranger saw this?

Practical rules

  • Use strong passwords and never share them.
  • Ask for help before joining new platforms or group chats.
  • Do not post images that reveal private information in the background.
  • Remember: screenshots exist, even if a post is deleted.

Misinformation and Fake News

Not everything online is true. Misinformation can spread quickly because posts are shared before people check them.

Check before you share

  • Who made it? Are they trustworthy?
  • What evidence is shown?
  • Is the headline trying to make you angry or shocked?
  • Can you confirm the story on another reliable site?

Cyberbullying and Harmful Contact

If something feels wrong, it probably is. Cyberbullying can happen in private messages, group chats, or online games.

If you need help: Save evidence, block/report the account, and talk to a trusted adult.
